## Bias

## Low wind events

 - Important at aggregate GB level for system operation and security of supply.
 - We define low wind events as periods of time when the total GB wind power generation is below a certain threshold (e.g., 5% of installed capacity).
 - We can analyze the distribution of these events in terms of their duration, frequency, and severity (e.g., cumulative shortfall).
 - We can also compare the observed low wind events with those simulated by the ERA5 reanalysis data to assess the accuracy of the reanalysis in capturing these events.
 - Ideally we'll model shortfall events, considering demand and other generation sources, but for now we focus on wind generation only.
